text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) has prepared a bill for the financing of political parties.
- Value Added Tax will be paid on transfers of soccer players between clubs.
- The government wishes to sell off state chemical firm Quimigal for seven billion escudos.
- Turnover of Portuguese insurance industry 822 billion escudos in 1996, up 17.2 percent compared with 1995.

- Alipio Dias steps down as head of Banco Totta & Acores and Credito Predial Portugues after nine years in charge and could be replaced by Luis Champalimaud, son of Antonio Champalimaud, who owns the banks.
